newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN says 14 Iraq oil inspectors already in place.
newsitem.headline: UN says 14 Iraq oil inspectors already in place.

text.p: In notifying the president of the Security Council Monday that the Iraqi "oil-for-food" deal is ready to be implemented, Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said the 14 inspectors who will monitor the oil flows were already in place.

"I authorized the dispatch of the 14 independent inspection agents from Saybolt to their designated duty stations at the Mina al-Bakr oil terminal, the pipeline metering station near Zakho and at the Ceyhan oil terminal. They have since been deployed to their duty stations," he added, referring to inspectors from the Dutch-based Saybolt company.

Most of the $2 billion worth of oil which Iraq is authorized to export over a six-month period will flow through a pipeline from Iraq to Turkey while the rest is to go via the Iraqi Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr.
The metering station near Zakho is on the Iraqi-Turkish border while Ceyhan is the terminal in Turkey.

Boutros-Ghali also said he had authorized an initial 13 inspection agents from Lloyd's Register, out of a total of 32 who will confirm the arrival of humanitarian goods, to proceed to Iraq. The remaining 19 would be sent as soon as it became operationally necessary, he added.

In his 1 1/2 page report to council President Francesco Paolo Fulci of Italy, Boutros-Ghali said: "I am satisfied that all the actions necessary to ensure the effective implementation of resolution 986 (1995) have been concluded."

That is the resolution, adopted in April last year, which provides authorization for the "oil-for-food" deal concluded by the United Nations and Iraq on May 20 this year but delayed due to differences over how it should be implemented.

The deal is renewable if the Security Council considers it is working as planned. The purpose is to enable Iraq to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods to help offset the effects of crippling sanctions in place since shortly after its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Boutros-Ghali added that the U.N. secretariat "stands ready to carry out its responsibilities as of 0001 Eastern Standard Time on the day after the president of the Security Council has informed the members of the council that he has received the present report, in accordance with the decision of the council in paragraph 3 of resolution 986 (1995)."
Council members met behind closed-doors Monday afternoon.
